arabic_blocks: [59] حدثنا محمد بن سنان قال: حدثنا فليح ح وحدثني إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا محمد بن فليح قال: حدثني أبي قال: حدثني هلال بن علي عن عطاء بن يسار عن أبي هريرة قال:

بينما النبي ﷺ في مجلس يحدث القوم جاءه أعرابي، فقال متى الساعة فمضى رسول الله ﷺ يحدث، فقال بعض القوم سمع ما قال: فكره ما قال، وقال بعضهم بل لم يسمع حتى إذا قضى حديثه قال أين أراه السائل عن الساعة؟ قال: ها أنا يا رسول الله قال: فإذا ضيعت الأمانة فانتظر الساعة قال كيف إضاعتها قال إذا وسد الأمر إلى غير أهله فانتظر الساعة
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Fulayh related to us.

Another chain: And Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Fulayh related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Hilal ibn ‘Ali related to me, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in a gathering speaking to the people, a Bedouin came to him and said: “When is the Hour?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, continued speaking. Some of the people said: “He heard what he said and disliked what he said.” Others said: “Rather, he did not hear.” When he finished speaking, he said: “Where—I think—is the one who asked about the Hour?” He said: “Here I am, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “When the trust is lost, await the Hour.” He said: “How is it lost?” He said: “When authority is entrusted to those unfit for it, await the Hour.”
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Both chain routes and the change-of-chain marker remain. The selected Arabic and modern print have Muhammad ibn Fulayh say “my father related to me”; the historical print has “related to us”. The selected singular is retained.

The selected digital phrase أين أراه السائل contains أراه between “where” and “the questioner”. Both printed witnesses omit this word here, as do the two English comparisons. The provisional “I think” preserves it as an interruption without assigning the uncertainty to a particular narrator. Its reading and speaker remain unresolved; the Arabic is not silently corrected.

The two differing audience reactions, the first reply about the trust, the follow-up question and the final condition all remain. “Authority” is provisional for الأمر in this context; no modern political application is added.

تخلف عنا النبي ﷺ في سفرة سافرناها فأدركنا وقد أرهقتنا الصلاة ونحن نتوضأ فجعلنا نمسح على أرجلنا فنادى بأعلى صوته ويل للأعقاب من النار مرتين أو ثلاثا

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed behind us on a journey we made. He caught up with us when the prayer was pressing upon us, while we were performing ablution. We began wiping our feet, and he called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire!” two or three times.

arabic_blocks: [63] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الليث عن سعيد هو المقبري عن شريك بن عبد الله بن أبي نمر أنه سمع أنس بن مالك يقول:

بينما نحن جلوس مع النبي ﷺ في المسجد دخل رجل على جمل فأناخه في المسجد ثم عقله، ثم قال لهم أيكم محمد والنبي ﷺ متكئ بين ظهرانيهم فقلنا هذا الرجل الأبيض المتكئ، فقال له الرجل بن عبد المطلب، فقال له النبي ﷺ قد أجبتك، فقال الرجل للنبي ﷺ إني سائلك فمشدد عليك في المسألة فلا تجد علي في نفسك، فقال سل عما بدا لك، فقال أسألك بربك ورب من قبلك آلله أرسلك إلى الناس كلهم، فقال اللهم نعم قال: أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن نصلي الصلوات الخمس في اليوم والليلة قال اللهم نعم قال: أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن نصوم هذا الشهر من السنة قال اللهم نعم قال: أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن تأخذ هذه الصدقة من أغنيائنا فتقسمها على فقرائنا، فقال النبي ﷺ اللهم نعم، فقال الرجل آمنت بما جئت به وأنا رسول من ورائي من قومي وأنا ضِمام بن ثعلبة أخو بني سعد بن بكر
رواه موسى وعلي بن عبد الحميد عن سليمان عن ثابت عن أنس عن النبي ﷺ بهذا.

While we were sitting with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque, a man entered on a camel. He made it kneel in the mosque and then hobbled it. Then he said to them: “Which of you is Muhammad?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was reclining among them. We said: “This fair-skinned man who is reclining.” The man said to him: “Son of ‘Abd al-Muttalib!” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “I have answered you.” The man said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “I am going to question you and be insistent in questioning you, so do not feel anger toward me.” He said: “Ask whatever occurs to you.” He said: “I ask you by your Lord and the Lord of those before you: did Allah send you to all people?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you that we should perform the five prayers in the day and night?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you that we should fast this month of the year?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you to take this charity from our rich and distribute it among our poor?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Allah, yes.” The man said: “I believe in what you have brought. I am a messenger from those of my people whom I have left behind. I am Dimam ibn Tha‘labah, a member of Banu Sa‘d ibn Bakr.”
Musa and ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid transmitted this report from Sulayman, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

When he read it, he tore it up. I think Ibn al-Musayyab said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed against them that they should be utterly torn apart.

He said: “Is it not Dhu al-Hijjah?” We said: “Yes.” He said: “Your blood, your property and your honour are sacred among you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours. arabic_blocks: [87] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا غندر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي جمرة قال: كنت أترجم بين بن عباس وبين الناس، فقال:

إن وفد عبد القيس أتوا النبي ﷺ، فقال من الوفد أو من القوم قالوا ربيعة، فقال مرحبا بالقوم أو بالوفد غير خزايا ولا ندامى قالوا إنا نأتيك من شقة بعيدة وبيننا وبينك هذا الحي من كفار مضر ولا نستطيع أن نأتيك إلا في شهر حرام فمرنا بأمر نخبر به من وراءنا ندخل به الجنة فأمرهم بأربع ونهاهم عن أربع أمرهم بالإيمان بالله عز وجل وحده قال هل تدرون ما الإيمان بالله وحده قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وصوم رمضان وتعطوا الخمس من المغنم ونهاهم عن الدباء والحنتم والمزفت قال شعبة ربما قال النقير وربما قال المقير قال احفظوه وأخبروه من وراءكم
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Jamrah, who said:
I used to interpret between Ibn ‘Abbas and the people. He said:

The delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: “Who is the delegation—or the people?” They said: “Rabi‘ah.” He said: “Welcome to the people—or the delegation—without disgrace or regret.” They said: “We come to you from a distant place. Between us and you is this group of the unbelievers of Mudar, and we can come to you only in a sacred month. Give us an instruction to convey to those we left behind, by which we may enter Paradise.” He instructed them in four things and forbade them four things. He instructed them to believe in Allah, mighty and majestic, alone. He said: “Do you know what belief in Allah alone is?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, fasting Ramadan, and giving the fifth of the spoils.” He forbade them al-dubba’, al-hantam and al-muzaffat.
Shu‘bah said: Sometimes he said al-naqir, and sometimes he said al-muqayyar.
He said: “Remember it and convey it to those you left behind.”

english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Muqatil Abu al-Hasan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: ‘Umar ibn Sa‘id ibn Abi Husayn informed us. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah related to me, from ‘Uqbah ibn al-Harith:

He married a daughter of Abu Ihab ibn ‘Aziz. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

I and a neighbour of mine from the Ansar were among Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, in the upper districts of Medina. We took turns going down to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: he would go one day and I another. When I went down, I brought him that day’s news of revelation and other matters; when he went down, he did the same. My Ansari companion went down on his day and then knocked hard at my door. He said: “Is he there?” I was alarmed and came out to him. He said: “A grave event has happened.” He said: I went in to Hafsah and found her weeping. I said: “Has the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, divorced you all?” She said: “I do not know.” Then I went in to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and, while standing, said: “Have you divorced your wives?” He said: “No.” I said: “Allah is greatest.”

He said: “People, you drive others away. Whoever leads people in prayer should make it light, for among them are the sick, the weak and those with a need.”

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amir related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Bilal al-Madini related to us, from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd, from Yazid, the mawla of al-Munba‘ith, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani:
A man asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about a lost article. He said: “Recognize its tying cord—
Or he said: its vessel.
—and its container. Then announce it for a year, then make use of it. If its owner comes, return it to him.” He said: “What about a stray camel?” He became angry until his cheeks reddened—
Or he said: his face reddened.

arabic_blocks: [112] حدثنا أبو نعيم الفضل بن دكين قال: حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة أن خزاعة قتلوا رجلا من بني ليث عام فتح مكة بقتيل منهم قتلوه فأخبر بذلك النبي ﷺ فركب راحلته فخطب، فقال إن الله حبس عن مكة القتل أو الفيل شك أبو عبد الله وسلط عليهم رسول الله ﷺ والمؤمنين ألا وإنها لم تحل لأحد قبلي ولم تحل لأحد بعدي ألا وإنها حلت لي ساعة من نهار ألا وإنها ساعتي هذه حرام لا يختلى شوكها ولا يعضد شجرها ولا تلتقط ساقطتها إلا لمنشد فمن قتل فهو بخير النظرين إما أن يعقل وإما أن يقاد أهل القتيل فجاء رجل من أهل اليمن، فقال اكتب لي يا رسول الله، فقال اكتبوا لأبي فلان، فقال رجل من قريش إلا الإذخر يا رسول الله فإنا نجعله في بيوتنا وقبورنا، فقال النبي ﷺ إلا الإذخر إلا الإذخر قال أبو عبد الله يقال يقاد بالقاف فقيل لأبي عبد الله أي شيء كتب له قال كتب له هذه الخطبة
english_blocks: Abu Nu‘aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

Khuza‘ah killed a man from Banu Layth in the year of the conquest of Mecca, in retaliation for one of their people whom they had killed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was informed of this, so he mounted his riding animal and delivered an address. He said: “Allah held back killing—or the elephant—from Mecca.”
Abu ‘Abdullah was uncertain.

“And He gave the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the believers power over them. Indeed, it was not made lawful for anyone before me, nor has it been made lawful for anyone after me. Indeed, it was made lawful for me for an hour of a day. Indeed, at this very hour of mine it is sacred: its thorns are not to be cut, its trees are not to be cut down, and its fallen property is not to be picked up except by someone who announces it. If someone is killed, there is a choice between two courses: blood money is paid, or retaliation is carried out for the family of the person killed.”

A man from Yemen came and said: “Write it down for me, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Write it for Abu so-and-so.” A man from Quraysh said: “Except idhkhir, Messenger of Allah, for we put it in our houses and graves.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Except idhkhir, except idhkhir.”
Abu ‘Abdullah said: “Yuqad is said with the letter qaf.” Abu ‘Abdullah was asked: “What was written for him?” He said: “This address was written for him.”

arabic_blocks: [114] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثني ابن وهب قال: أخبرني يونس عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله عن ابن عباس قال لما اشتد بالنبي ﷺ وجعه قال ائتوني بكتاب أكتب لكم كتابا لا تضلوا بعده قال عمر إن النبي ﷺ غلبه الوجع وعندنا كتاب الله حسبنا فاختلفوا وكثر اللغط قال قوموا عني ولا ينبغي عندي التنازع فخرج بن عباس يقول إن الرزية كل الرزية ما حال بين رسول الله ﷺ وبين كتابه
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

When the pain of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became severe, he said: “Bring me writing material so that I may write you a document after which you will not go astray.” ‘Umar said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is overcome by pain, and we have the Book of Allah; it is enough for us.” They disagreed, and the clamour increased. He said: “Leave me. Disputing in my presence is not fitting.” Ibn ‘Abbas went out saying: “The calamity, the whole calamity, was what came between the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his writing.”

english_blocks: Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to me. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim and Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the ‘Isha’ prayer near the end of his life. When he had given the salutation, he stood and said: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of one hundred years from it, none of those now on the face of the earth will remain.”

arabic_blocks: [117] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا الحكم قال: سمعت سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال بت في بيت خالتي ميمونة بنت الحارث زوج النبي ﷺ وكان النبي ﷺ عندها في ليلتها فصلى النبي ﷺ العشاء ثم جاء إلى منزله فصلى أربع ركعات ثم نام ثم قام، ثم قال نام الغليم أو كلمة تشبهها ثم قام فقمت عن يساره فجعلني عن يمينه فصلى خمس ركعات ثم صلى ركعتين ثم نام حتى سمعت غطيطه أو خطيطه ثم خرج إلى الصلاة

I spent the night in the house of my maternal aunt Maymunah bint al-Harith, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was with her on her night. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Isha’, then came to his home and prayed four rak‘ahs, then slept. Then he rose and said: “Has the little boy slept?”—or a similar expression. Then he stood, and I stood on his left, so he placed me on his right. He prayed five rak‘ahs, then prayed two rak‘ahs, then slept until I heard his snoring—ghatit, or khatit—then went out to the prayer.

arabic_blocks: [118] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثني مالك عن ابن شهاب عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة قال إن الناس يقولون أكثر أبو هريرة ولولا آيتان في كتاب الله ما حدثت حديثا ثم يتلو { إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات } إلى قوله { الرحيم } إن إخواننا من المهاجرين كان يشغلهم الصفق بالأسواق وإن إخواننا من الأنصار كان يشغلهم العمل في أموالهم وإن أبا هريرة كان يلزم رسول الله ﷺ بشبع بطنه ويحضر ما لا يحضرون ويحفظ ما لا يحفظون
english_blocks: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:
“People say: ‘Abu Hurayrah has related a great deal.’ Were it not for two verses in the Book of Allah, I would not have related a single hadith.”
Then he recites: “Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs,” up to His words, “the Merciful.”

“Our brothers among the emigrants were kept busy by trading in the markets, and our brothers among the Ansar were kept busy by work on their property. Abu Hurayrah would remain with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, content with enough to fill his stomach. He would attend what they did not attend and retain what they did not retain.”

arabic_blocks: [122] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا عمرو قال: أخبرني سعيد بن جبير قال: قلت لابن عباس إن نوفا البكالي يزعم أن موسى ليس بموسى بني إسرائيل إنما هو موسى آخر، فقال كذب عدوالله حدثنا أبي بن كعب عن النبي ﷺ قام موسى النبي خطيبا في بني إسرائيل فسئل أي الناس أعلم، فقال: أنا أعلم فعتب الله عليه إذ لم يرد العلم إليه فأوحى الله إليه إن عبدا من عبادي بمجمع البحرين هو أعلم منك قال: يا رب وكيف به فقيل له احمل حوتا في مكتل فإذا فقدته فهو ثم فانطلق وانطلق بفتاه يوشع بن نون وحمل حوتا في مكتل حتى كانا عند الصخرة وضعا رؤوسهما وناما فانسل الحوت من المكتل { فاتخذ سبيله في البحر سربا } وكان لموسى وفتاه عجبا فانطلقا بقية ليلتهما ويومهما فلما أصبح قال موسى لفتاه { آتنا غداءنا لقد لقينا من سفرنا هذا نصبا } ولم يجد موسى مسا من النصب حتى جاوز المكان الذي أمر به، فقال له فتاه { أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة فإني نسيت الحوت } قال موسى { ذلك ما كنا نبغي فارتدا على آثارهما قصصا } فلما انتهيا إلى الصخرة إذا رجل مسجى بثوب أو قال تسجى بثوبه فسلم موسى، فقال الخضر وأنى بأرضك السلام، فقال: أنا موسى، فقال موسى بني إسرائيل قال: نعم قال { هل أتبعك على أن تعلمني مما علمت رشدا } قال { إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا } يا موسى إني على علم من علم الله علمنيه لا تعلمه أنت وأنت على علم علمكه لا أعلمه { قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا } فانطلقا يمشيان على ساحل البحر ليس لهما سفينة فمرت بهما سفينة فكلموهم أن يحملوهما فعرف الخضر فحملوهما بغير نول فجاء عصفور فوقع على حرف السفينة فنقر نقرة أو نقرتين في البحر، فقال الخضر يا موسى ما نقص علمي وعلمك من علم الله إلا كنقرة هذا العصفور في البحر فعمد الخضر إلى لوح من ألواح السفينة فنزعه، فقال موسى قوم حملونا بغير نول عمدت إلى سفينتهم فخرقتها لتغرق أهلها { قال ألم أقل إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا قال لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت } فكانت الأولى من موسى نسيانا فانطلقا فإذا غلام يلعب مع الغلمان فأخذ الخضر برأسه من أعلاه فاقتلع رأسه بيده، فقال موسى { أقتلت نفسا زكية بغير نفس } { قال ألم أقل لك إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا } قال ابن عيينة وهذا أوكد { فانطلقا حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فأقامه } قال الخضر بيده فأقامه، فقال له موسى { لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا قال هذا فراق بيني وبينك } قال النبي ﷺ يرحم الله موسى لوددنا لو صبر حتى يقص علينا من أمرهما
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr related to us. He said: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr informed me. He said:
I said to Ibn ‘Abbas: “Nawf al-Bakali claims that Musa was not the Musa of the Children of Israel, but another Musa.” He said: “The enemy of Allah has lied.”
Ubayy ibn Ka‘b related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Musa the prophet stood to address the Children of Israel. He was asked: ‘Which person has the most knowledge?’ He said: ‘I have the most knowledge.’ Allah reproached him because he had not referred knowledge to Him. Allah revealed to him: ‘A servant of Mine at the meeting of the two seas has more knowledge than you.’ He said: ‘My Lord, how can I reach him?’ He was told: ‘Carry a fish in a basket. When you lose it, he will be there.’

“He set out with his young companion, Yusha‘ ibn Nun, carrying a fish in a basket. When they reached the rock, they laid down their heads and slept. The fish slipped out of the basket and ‘took its way into the sea as through a tunnel.’ It was a wonder to Musa and his young companion. They travelled on for the rest of their night and day. When morning came, Musa said to his young companion: ‘Bring us our meal; we have suffered weariness from this journey of ours.’ Musa had felt no weariness until he passed the place to which he had been directed. His young companion said to him: ‘Do you remember when we sheltered at the rock? I forgot the fish.’ Musa said: ‘That is what we were seeking.’ ‘So they returned, retracing their footsteps.’

“When they reached the rock, there was a man covered with a garment—or he said: he had covered himself with his garment. Musa greeted him. Al-Khadir said: ‘How is there this greeting in your land?’ He said: ‘I am Musa.’ He said: ‘Musa of the Children of Israel?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘May I follow you so that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?’ He said: ‘You will not be able to be patient with me. Musa, I have knowledge from Allah’s knowledge which He taught me and which you do not know, and you have knowledge He taught you which I do not know.’ ‘He said: You will find me patient, if Allah wills, and I will not disobey you in any matter.’

“They set off walking along the seashore, without a boat. A boat passed them, and they spoke to its people to take them aboard. Al-Khadir was recognised, and they carried them without a fare. A sparrow came and settled on the edge of the boat, dipping its beak once or twice into the sea. Al-Khadir said: ‘Musa, my knowledge and your knowledge have diminished Allah’s knowledge only as this sparrow’s dipping has diminished the sea.’

“Al-Khadir went to one of the boat’s planks and pulled it out. Musa said: ‘People carried us without a fare, and you have gone to their boat and made a hole in it to drown its people!’ ‘He said: Did I not say that you would not be able to be patient with me?’ ‘He said: Do not take me to task for what I forgot.’ Musa’s first lapse was forgetfulness.

“They went on, and there was a boy playing with other boys. Al-Khadir took hold of the top of his head and pulled his head off with his hand. Musa said: ‘Have you killed an innocent soul, without its having killed a soul?’ ‘He said: Did I not say to you that you would not be able to be patient with me?’”
Ibn ‘Uyaynah said: “This is more emphatic.”

“They went on until, when they came to the people of a village, they asked its people for food, but they refused to give them hospitality. They found there a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright.” Al-Khadir gestured with his hand and set it upright. Musa said to him: “Had you wished, you could have taken payment for it.” “He said: This is the parting between me and you.”
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “May Allah have mercy on Musa. We would have wished that he had been patient, so that more of their affair would have been related to us.”

A man asked him: “What does a person in ihram wear?” He said: “He does not wear a shirt, a turban, trousers, a hooded cloak, or a garment touched by wars or saffron. If he cannot find sandals, let him wear leather socks and cut them so that they are below the ankles.”
